title: api-config-runtime-fallback-routing-notes-jamie
content:
Context:
Small brain-dump on runtime-level fallback routing config. This is a personal scratchpad: short-term thing to get ideas down before turning into a PR/spec for the runtime config parser. Goal is to provide an expressive, minimal config shape that lets ops teams declare fallback policies (model variant fallback, region fallback, capacity-tier fallback) while keeping rules simple and predictable for autoscaling + routing layer.

Requirements / constraints:
- Express fallback priorities: e.g., model-variant -> region -> capacity-tier.
- Allow per-route overrides (different routes can have different tolerance for quality vs latency).
- Support percent-based fallback (e.g., 10% of traffic can be routed to a cheaper variant as trial).
- Observable: each fallback event should emit a structured reason (model_miss, capacity_shortage, latency_spike) and target used.
- Compatible with existing smart routing policies (latency-based, cost-based) — fallback is a policy that can be plugged in.
- Simple defaults so teams can opt-in without authoring a lot.

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- Should we treat model-variant fallback as first-class separate list, or as another rule type with match conditions? Pros: variant list makes it explicit. Cons: additional complexity in UI/console.
- How to express conditional fallback (only fallback to cheaper variant if median latency > X ms AND error-rate > Y)? We can support simple "conditions" with boolean ops but that increases parser needs. Maybe keep to simple thresholds for v1.
- Interaction with rollouts/canary: if rollouts already exist, fallback should avoid overriding rollout weighting. We'll need clear precedence rules.

Sketch: top-level route config with fallback block (YAML-like, simplified):

route: "/chat/completions"
method: POST
model: "gptx-4f/1.0"
fallback:
  enabled: true
  priority: ["model_variant", "region", "capacity_tier"]
  max_fallback_percent: 20   # global cap for this route
  rules:
    - id: model_variant_trial
      type: model_variant
      variants:
        - name: "gptx-4f-quantized"
          weight: 90
        - name: "gptx-4f-int8-cheap"
          weight: 10
      conditions:
        latency_ms_gt: 250   # only start fallback if p50 > 250ms
        error_rate_gt: 0.02  # and error rate > 2%
    - id: regional_failover
      type: region
      targets: ["us-west-2", "us-east-1"]
      conditions:
        capacity_utilization_gt: 0.9
    - id: capacity_tier_burst
      type: capacity_tier
      targets: ["on-demand", "preemptible"]
      percent: 100  # allow full fallback to lower tier when needed

Notes on semantics:
- priority array controls the order of attempts. For each request: try primary model/region/tier, if it fails (timeout, service-unavailable, quota) then evaluate first matching rule in priority order and attempt routing accordingly.
- percent fields are enforced per-route as a rolling counter (to avoid sudden switchovers). We need a distributed counter or sampling token approach. Simplest: sampling by hashing request ID against threshold; easier to implement but less exact.
- conditions evaluated on recent metrics (sliding window). Need to pick default window (1m or 5m).

Telemetry / observability:
- Emit events: fallback.attempted, fallback.succeeded, fallback.degraded. Fields: route, rule_id, reason, src_model, dst_model, latency_ms, trace_id, sample_id.
- Add metrics: fallback_attempts_total{route,rule_id,result}, fallback_latency_histogram. Also a gauge for current_fallback_percent per-route.

Edge cases / failure modes:
- Flapping: repeated fallback toggles can cause instability. Mitigation: cooldown period per-rule (e.g., 30s) and backoff multiplier.
- Conflicting rollouts: if a model rollout is in progress, fallback must respect rollout traffic splits. Document precedence and maybe error out if config conflicts.
- Partial failures: if fallback target fails, ensure we circuit-break and move to next rule.

Implementation notes / next steps:
- Minimal parser: accept YAML/JSON route config with fallback block. Validate semantics server-side.
- Sampling: start with deterministic hash sampling for percent-based fallback; later we can add distributed counters if needed.
- Metrics: add structured logs/events ASAP so we can observe behavior during canary.
- UI: need simple toggles for enabled + priority order; advanced rule editor for conditions/variants.

TODO (for PR/spec):
- [ ] Finalize config schema (decide whether conditions are simple thresholds only)
- [ ] Add explicit precedence section for rollout interactions
- [ ] Draft telemetry format (fields, metric names)
- [ ] Spike deterministic sampling implementation and test in staging
- [ ] Write unit tests for parser and rule evaluation engine

Rough ASCII flow (request path):
  + incoming request -> route match -> evaluate primary target -> success? -> yes -> done
                                           -> no -> check fallback.enabled -> if false -> return error
                                           -> iterate priority list -> for each rule evaluate conditions -> if match -> select target -> attempt -> success? -> stop; else continue to next rule -> if none match -> final error

Notes to self: keep the first PR small: model_variant with simple percent sampling + cooldown + telemetry. Defer complex condition language to v2.

End of notes.
